findings.issue: Anonymous load amplification. One public `GET /api/products/batch?detail=true` with 50 ids runs a detail build per product: images, variants and OfferService.enrich, which makes about one inventory stock-rows call per product. The lean batch did 2 queries and `/{id}` does about 1 enrich per request. Under the edge limit of 300 reads per minute per subject or IP, one anonymous client can now drive about 15k inventory calls per minute instead of about 300.
findings.fix: Already tracked as TD-BE-18 (batched stock-rows endpoint). Until then, consider a tighter gateway read bucket for `detail=true`, or limiting detail mode to authenticated callers, since order-service always forwards the user's bearer.

findings.issue: findDetailsByIds applies no active or moderation filter, so inactive and unapproved (PENDING or REJECTED) products are returned to anonymous callers along with their full detail fields, such as moderationStatus and moderationNote. This matches `/{id}` exactly (findById at line 388 calls detail() unfiltered, and SecurityConfig permits GET /api/products/** to everyone), so it is not a new field exposure. It does add a bulk read path. Enumeration is not practical because ids are random UUIDv4 and the cap is 50.
findings.fix: No change needed for this PR. It is recorded as TD-BE-17 for the Owner. If the Owner decides to hide these products, gate inactive or unapproved items behind a service or admin token in both `/{id}` and the batch, and consider leaving moderationNote out of the public view.

summary: I checked the CTO's ruling (b) against the code and it holds. `GET /api/products/{id}` is public (product-service SecurityConfig permits GET /api/products/**, with admin paths carved out). It returns any product, inactive or unapproved included, through the same detail() builder that `detail=true` now uses with withStock=false. The parity integration test also shows the inactive HEADSET coming back 200 from `/{id}`. So the batch exposes no field beyond `/{id}`, and it actually shows less stock data because availableQuantity is left empty. The 50-id cap and the per-element UUID.fromString validation (400) apply in both modes and are tested. Duplicates are collapsed. The ids reach only findAllById as typed UUIDs, so there is no SQL or JPQL injection. On the order side, the csv is built from server-side UUID.toString values, so header or query injection is not possible. Prices stay server-authoritative: unit prices, names and images come only from the product-service view (base, variant or offer chosen server-side). Client cart price and name are ignored, which AC-12 tests. Ids missing from the response are refused with PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE before any order row, and unrequested ids returned by product-service are ignored. ProductBatchFeignClient has no `configuration=InternalFeignConfig`, so X-Internal-Token is never attached. Only the caller's Authorization header is relayed by CorrelationAndAuthForwardingInterceptor, and only to in-cluster targets; a test checks this. The new ORDER_PRODUCT_BATCH_READ_TIMEOUT_MS is a non-secret numeric setting with a 5000 ms default, and connect timeout stays at 1 s. There are no new dependencies, secrets or PII in logs. My two minor findings cover the anonymous amplification and bulk inactive-product reads, both already in the backlog as TD-BE-18 and TD-BE-17. There are no blockers or majors.
